developer.title: Developer feedback
developer.purpose: Cheap source and stable-reference checks suitable for routine edits.

pr.title: Pull-request evidence
pr.purpose: Durable implementation, conformance, policy, and static-quality checks used at the public integration boundary.

research-checkpoint.title: Research checkpoint
research-checkpoint.purpose: Bounded semantic witnesses and falsifiers used when closing a coherent redesign boundary.

scheduled.title: Scheduled deep checks
scheduled.purpose: Broader research reruns and diagnostics whose latency is unsuitable for edit-time feedback.

release-freeze.title: Release or specification freeze
release-freeze.purpose: All locally executable durable and bounded research checks, including the canonical expensive Analysis run.

formal-reading.title: Pinned formal reading
formal-reading.purpose: Externally provisioned reading of formalization receipts against the pinned upstream checkout.

checks.title: Check-control self-tests
checks.subject: The manifest parser, selector, command resolver, and structured result writer.
checks.claim: The checked control-plane invariants hold for the committed manifest and synthetic runner cases.
nonclaims: This does not validate the semantics or implementation exercised by any child check.

checks.title: Public-tree boundary
checks.subject: Repository paths forbidden from the public source tree.
checks.claim: No tracked path violates the public-tree policy encoded by the guard.
nonclaims: A passing guard does not classify untracked files or establish document authority.

checks.title: Python semantic-reference self-check
checks.subject: The durable Python semantic twin and its embedded known-answer and negative cases.
checks.claim: The reference package accepts and rejects its committed bounded corpus as declared.
nonclaims: Self-consistency is not independence from the specification or the C++ implementation.

checks.title: Python defect lint
checks.subject: Tracked Python sources under the repository-wide Ruff policy.
checks.claim: The selected static defect rules report no finding.
nonclaims: Lint success is not functional, semantic, security, or style completeness.

checks.title: Rust emitter unit suites
checks.subject: The Rust emitter workspace package.
checks.claim: The emitter unit and integration cases pass under the locked dependency graph.
nonclaims: The selected Rust cases do not establish backend correctness for all inputs.

checks.title: Rust runtime integration suites
checks.subject: The runtime package under its toy and pinned-upstream feature surfaces.
checks.claim: The selected runtime cases pass under the locked dependency graph.
nonclaims: The selected feature cases do not establish general runtime or upstream conformance.

checks.title: Rust static analysis
checks.subject: All Rust workspace targets and features under Clippy.
checks.claim: Clippy reports no warning under the configured locked workspace.
nonclaims: Static-analysis success is not functional or semantic correctness.

checks.title: Rust formatting
checks.subject: Rust workspace source formatting.
checks.claim: Rustfmt would make no change to the workspace sources.
nonclaims: Formatting success carries no behavioral claim.

checks.title: C++ and MLIR compiler suite
checks.subject: The configured native build's lit suite and four pure-core unit executables.
checks.claim: The configured build passes the committed compiler, tool, differential, and unit corpus.
nonclaims: Corpus success is not compiler correctness, protocol security, or production readiness.

checks.title: Pinned formalization-receipt reading
checks.subject: Declared formalization receipts read against the pinned ArkLib checkout.
checks.claim: The external workflow can classify the receipts against the exact pinned source revision.
nonclaims: A successful reading is not a compiler-build result, runtime input, or proof of every project claim.

checks.title: Cross-owner semantic closure
checks.subject: The bounded cross-owner semantic closure research model.
checks.claim: The committed finite closure cases satisfy their declared structural and identity laws.
nonclaims: This finite research model is not a product implementation or a semantic completeness proof.

checks.title: Semantic-profile publication
checks.subject: The indexed target-profile publication model and independent compiler.
checks.claim: Both finite publication paths agree on the committed profiles and reject the selected mutations.
nonclaims: Publication agreement is not target evaluator, theorem, or runtime conformance evidence.

checks.title: Recursive-composition boundary
checks.subject: The finite owner-boundary model for recursive composition.
checks.claim: The selected composition shapes preserve the declared ownership and handoff constraints.
nonclaims: This is not a recursion implementation or an IVC, PCD, or preservation theorem.

checks.title: Executable foundations
checks.subject: The constitutional value, identity, term, and outcome research surface.
checks.claim: The finite foundation model and independent identity oracle satisfy the frozen cases.
nonclaims: The bounded model does not decode every request carrier or establish protocol or cryptographic claims.

checks.title: Interactive protocol and Fiat-Shamir contracts
checks.subject: The bounded InteractiveCore, transcript-binding, and Fiat-Shamir contract model.
checks.claim: The selected positive and adversarial cases satisfy the declared protocol and transform laws.
nonclaims: Finite transcript cases do not prove Fiat-Shamir security, soundness, or concrete-hash security.

checks.title: Interface, Plan, and Relations surfaces
checks.subject: The bounded semantic surfaces downstream of the interactive protocol core.
checks.claim: The selected finite owner views and cross-surface handoffs obey their declared laws.
nonclaims: Finite surface closure is not general protocol-family support or implementation conformance.

checks.title: Indexed Core elaboration
checks.subject: The bounded static finite-repeat authoring grammar and elaboration model.
checks.claim: The finite indexed programs elaborate to admitted concrete Cores within declared structural bounds.
nonclaims: Bounded elaboration is not an all-index theorem or dynamic-topology support.

checks.title: Plan continuation semantics
checks.subject: Finite accumulation, folding, and recursion continuation shapes.
checks.claim: The selected shapes respect Plan-owned decisions, grounding, one-use handoff, and endpoint derivation.
nonclaims: The finite adapter model is not a protocol implementation, recurrence proof, or security result.

checks.title: Duplex transcript construction
checks.subject: The finite overwrite-duplex transcript construction and replay model.
checks.claim: The construction, transition, provenance, replay, and mutation cases reproduce the frozen projection.
nonclaims: The finite construction does not prove random-oracle, sponge, or concrete-permutation security.

checks.title: Native FRI and logical Oracle
checks.subject: One finite logical-oracle FRI construction, execution, grounding, and analysis-question path.
checks.claim: The source-bound public replay and independent selected facts agree for the declared finite case.
nonclaims: One finite case is not general FRI, construction-admission, paper-correspondence, theorem, or security evidence.

checks.title: Property Analysis closure
checks.subject: The canonical one-process bounded property-analysis research suite.
checks.claim: All discovered finite Analysis cases pass in one process against one reconstructed state.
nonclaims: The finite suite is not theorem truth, theorem applicability, cryptographic security, or implementation conformance.

checks.title: Endpoint projection
checks.subject: The bounded source-relative PIR-to-OIR projection model.
checks.claim: The selected source graph, admitted endpoint graph, quotient, and mismatch cases satisfy the declared projection boundary.
nonclaims: Finite graph agreement is not full OIR syntax, refinement, execution, or family support.

checks.title: Joined semantic boundary
checks.subject: The finite joined protocol, dependent-surface, Analysis, and endpoint path.
checks.claim: The selected total-uniform Schnorr-shaped path closes under exact shared identities and owner APIs.
nonclaims: The joined finite witness is not general authority implementation, theorem truth, or security evidence.

checks.title: Retained Schnorr portfolio witness
checks.subject: The source-bound finite Fresh and Fiat-Shamir Schnorr portfolio case.
checks.claim: The public rebuild, exact report verification, frozen projection, and replay all agree for the retained finite scope.
nonclaims: The retained finite case is not a cryptographic theorem or complete diagnostic-reachability result.

checks.title: FRI grinding residual witness
checks.subject: The repaired finite FRI grinding fixture through its pre-opening stopping point.
checks.claim: The frozen replay corpus and local tests agree through the declared residual boundary.
nonclaims: The witness stops before authenticated FRI opening and acceptance and is not a native FRI case.

checks.title: Finite logical-program cover
checks.subject: The finite logical-program cover analysis and independent oracle.
checks.claim: The selected finite covers and refusals agree across the primary model and independent arithmetic path.
nonclaims: Finite cover evidence is not a theorem over all programs or target-Core admission evidence.

checks.title: Verifier-derived query plans
checks.subject: The bounded nonadaptive query-plan elaboration and independent oracle.
checks.claim: The finite query plans elaborate into the declared flat Core behavior and reject selected invalid shapes.
nonclaims: Static elaboration evidence is not a new runtime event, theorem applicability, or target support claim.

checks.title: Portable formal-source package
checks.subject: One finite portable source/read package and independent Python and Rust checkers.
checks.claim: The two checkers agree on the affirmative propositions and selected exact-class mutations.
nonclaims: Feasibility evidence is not live-owner correspondence, theorem truth, or product-format selection.

checks.title: Formal-source target basis
checks.subject: The exact target-profile basis and fixture-substitution discriminator.
checks.claim: Two publication compilers reconstruct the frozen target basis and reject the selected substitutions.
nonclaims: Profile/source closure is not a target body compiler, admission evaluator, owner-view evaluator, or implementation claim.

checks.title: Formal-source target Core
checks.subject: One exact finite target carrier and bounded admission evaluator.
checks.claim: The independent encoders, exhaustive equation inputs, and selected admission mutations agree for the target slice.
nonclaims: The finite target slice is not a complete evaluator, owner-view result, execution claim, or security result.

checks.title: Formal-source owner-view audit
checks.subject: Exact owner-view source determinacy at the published PIR boundary.
checks.claim: The audit deterministically classifies whether the committed source publishes enough material for exact owner-local reads.
nonclaims: A deterministic CannotAnswer result is not a target repair, owner-view evaluator, or defect in an admitted Core.

checks.title: Owner-view publication topology
checks.subject: A synthetic profile-local publication repair for owner-view source determinacy.
checks.claim: Two publication compilers agree on the selected owner, declaration, routing, dependency, and identity-rotation topology and reject the selected mutations.
nonclaims: Topology feasibility does not publish exact view grammars, migrate target identities, derive a view, establish correspondence, or verify implementation code.

checks.title: Canonical owner-view schema algebra
checks.subject: The finite structural and semantic-atom algebra proposed for six PIR owner views.
checks.claim: Recursive and iterative evaluators agree on the committed schema, value, manifest, and mutation cases.
nonclaims: Finite schema-algebra agreement is not an exact target body grammar, owner derivation, profile migration, source correspondence, or implementation result.

checks.title: Owner-view body source determinacy
checks.subject: The published source material required to define six exact PIR owner-view bodies.
checks.claim: The audit reproducibly classifies the committed prerequisites, missing definitions, and unsound repair routes.
nonclaims: A reproducible CannotAnswer classification is not a target repair, canonical body definition, derived view, source correspondence, or implementation result.

checks.title: Commitment and opening invariant probe
checks.subject: Cross-cutting finite commitment and opening invariants.
checks.claim: The selected positive and negative invariant probes behave as declared.
nonclaims: Cross-cutting probes are not a protocol portfolio case or general commitment security evidence.

checks.title: LogUp claim-routing invariant probe
checks.subject: Cross-cutting finite LogUp claim-routing invariants.
checks.claim: The selected positive and negative routing probes behave as declared.
nonclaims: Cross-cutting probes are not a protocol portfolio case or a LogUp theorem.

checks.title: Value-bridge invariant probe
checks.subject: Cross-cutting finite lossless and lossy value-bridge invariants.
checks.claim: The selected bridge and loss-accounting probes behave as declared.
nonclaims: Cross-cutting probes are not a protocol portfolio case or a general bridge theorem.

checks.title: Guard-cost invariant probe
checks.subject: Cross-cutting finite guard normalization and carrier-cost invariants.
checks.claim: The selected guard-equivalence and cost probes behave as declared.
nonclaims: Cross-cutting probes are not a protocol portfolio case or a worst-case complexity proof.

checks.title: Authored boundary-coverage snapshot
checks.subject: The manually curated mapping from research instruments to architectural boundaries.
checks.claim: The diagnostic can reproduce its current bounded coverage snapshot.
nonclaims: Authored coverage labels are review priorities, not closure verdicts or theorem coverage.

checks.title: Result-code reachability snapshot
checks.subject: Declared and fired result codes across the current research suites.
checks.claim: The instrumentation can reproduce the current declared-versus-fired snapshot.
nonclaims: A fired code does not discharge an invariant, and an unfired code is not automatically a defect.
